Job description

**Senior Wireless Network Consultant, Cisco Meraki**

**A large multinational enterprise is looking for an experienced wireless specialist to improve the reliability of its Cisco Meraki Wi-Fi network. The estate spans a very large number of sites worldwide, many in dense urban buildings with heavy RF interference. Users rely on the wireless network for voice and video conferencing, and the team wants to eliminate sporadic drops, roaming failures and degraded call quality.**

**You will be the regional technical lead for Asia-Pacific, working with a distributed engineering team across time zones.**

**The work**

* Review the existing Meraki setup (network templates, SSIDs, RF profiles, band steering, authentication, firmware) and find where sites have drifted from the intended configuration.
* Investigate intermittent client issues using Meraki dashboard data, event logs and packet captures, and trace them to root cause.
* Assess RF design in crowded and high-density locations, including channel width, transmit power and auto-RF limits, and mitigation of external interference.
* Define a clear, repeatable configuration baseline and a process for approving exceptions.
* Plan and supervise pilots before wider rollout, with defined success measures and a way to roll back. Shape a staged approach to firmware and configuration releases.
* Automate repetitive checks and fixes through the Meraki API, covering monitoring, self-healing actions and safe change deployment.
* Set the health indicators the network should be measured against (client failures, connection time, signal quality, channel utilisation, loss and latency) and improve how this data reaches existing monitoring tools.
* Write troubleshooting guides and runbooks, and train regional support engineers.
* Help clarify support tiers and how issues are escalated to Cisco/Meraki TAC when a high-severity case arises.
* Advise endpoint teams on client-side behaviour that affects wireless performance.

**What you bring**

* 10+ years in enterprise networking, including 6+ years centred on wireless
* Proven delivery on large, multi-site Cisco Meraki MR deployments
* Strong grounding in RF: channel planning, auto-RF behaviour, dense floor design, 5 GHz and 6 GHz
* Good command of roaming (802.11r/k/v), WPA2/WPA3, and 802.1X with RADIUS
* Practical experience diagnosing real-time audio/video performance over Wi-Fi (QoS/DSCP, airtime, retries)
* Knowledge of the wired side that affects APs: PoE, switch ports, STP, LACP, uplinks
* Scripting skills (Python or similar) and familiarity with the Meraki API
* Experience producing design standards, KPIs and operational documentation within formal change control
* Clear communication, including with senior stakeholders

**Helpful to have:**
CWAP, CWDP or CWNA; CCNP Enterprise (wireless); CCIE Enterprise Wireless; a Meraki certification; Cisco DevNet. Certifications should be current and verifiable.

* **To apply:**
  send your CV with notice period to kiran@crysol.com or apply on LinkedIn. Please mention the number of Meraki sites and APs you have handled and one concrete improvement in Wi-Fi stability that you delivered.

Alpha Data is modernising its enterprise Linux platform across Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and Oracle Enterprise Linux (OEL). **2.1 RHEL and OEL Modernisation**

* Define supported RHEL and OEL release baselines, upgrade paths, compatibility requirements and lifecycle controls.

**2.3 VMWare Platform Integration**

* Engineer and maintain RHEL/OEL VM templates, content libraries and build standards on VMware vSphere (ESXi / vCenter).
* Automate VM provisioning with Packer, Ansible (VMware collections), PowerCLI, Terraform and vSphere APIs, integrated with Satellite and CI/CD pipelines.

**2.4 Linux Build Automation and Integration**

* Integrate builds with DNS, NTP, NFS, SNMP, SMTP, Active Directory, TCP/IP, container registries, CI/CD pipelines, logging, monitoring, SIEM, backup and service-management tooling.

* Engineer hardware integration and firmware-management patterns for Dell and HPE server estates.

**2.5 Security, Performance and Resilience**

* Define and automate OS hardening standards with Information Security, covering access, logging, cryptography, privileged controls and audit settings.
* Engineer kernel, memory, CPU, I/O and network TCP tuning baselines, including workload-specific profiles and measurable performance checks.
* Define observability standards and dashboards for OS and hardware health, capacity, performance and configuration compliance.
* Provide Level 3 engineering expertise for defects attributable to the newly engineered platform during agreed pilot and early-life support windows.

**2.6 Engineering and Automation Lifecycle**

* Design, build, test and document automated deployment pipelines and reusable platform artefacts.
* Integrate pipelines and artefacts into the automation orchestration platform (HCL BigFix CLM / BigFix Runbook AI).
* Apply source control, peer review, release management and traceability to scripts, templates, configurations and images.
* Develop an integrated automated validation framework covering build completeness, configuration compliance, security controls, performance baselines and platform health, using AI tooling where appropriate.
* Define versioning, promotion, rollback, break-glass and exception-handling processes.
* Provide engineering support during controlled pilots and early-life adoption.

Expert-level RHEL and OEL engineering (builds, upgrades, lifecycle, kernel tuning, hardening).

Content views, lifecycle environments, subscriptions, patch channels and provisioning.

Kickstart, PXE, DHCP, Redfish and Packer for bare metal and virtual builds.

Strong Ansible (roles, collections, AAP/Tower), Bash and Python scripting.

OpenShift Virtualization, container image engineering, registries and image promotion.

Image engineering (Glance), cloud-init, flavours and integration with compute, network and storage services.

Strong hands-on vSphere 7/8 (ESXi, vCenter), VM templates and content libraries, vSAN, NSX / vDS networking, DRS / HA, and guest OS optimisation for Linux.

•     
**VMware automation:**
PowerCLI, vSphere APIs, Terraform vSphere provider, Packer vsphere-iso builder and Ansible VMware collections.

Git, peer review, pipelines (e.g. GitLab CI, Jenkins) and release management.

•     
**Enterprise integration:**
DNS, NTP, NFS, SNMP, SMTP, Active Directory / SSSD, logging, monitoring, SIEM and backup tooling.

**Security:**
CIS / DISA STIG hardening, OpenSCAP compliance scanning, privileged access and audit controls.

Dell iDRAC / OpenManage and HPE iLO / OneView, including firmware management.

**4. Desirable Skills**

Experience migrating VMware workloads to OpenShift Virtualization or OpenStack.

We are looking for a skilled System Administrator to manage, maintain and secure the organisation's IT infrastructure. The role involves administering servers, networks, enterprise systems and endpoint environments while ensuring high availability, security and seamless IT operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage and maintain Windows and Linux servers, operating systems and infrastructure.
* Administer Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, DNS, DHCP and Group Policies.
* Manage Microsoft 365, Exchange Online, user accounts and access permissions.
* Monitor server performance, system availability, backups and infrastructure health.
* Configure and troubleshoot LAN, WAN, VPN, Wi-Fi and network connectivity.
* Manage endpoint devices, antivirus, patch management and security updates.
* Implement backup, disaster recovery and business continuity procedures.
* Handle IT incidents, service requests and infrastructure troubleshooting.
* Manage IT asset inventory, software licences and hardware procurement.
* Coordinate with vendors and technology partners for infrastructure support.
* Maintain IT documentation, SOPs, access records and compliance requirements.
* Identify infrastructure risks and recommend improvements to system performance and security.

Required Technical Skills

* Strong hands-on experience with Windows Server and Linux administration.
* Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS and DHCP.
* Microsoft 365 and Entra ID administration.
* Networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, VPN, LAN and WAN.
* Virtualisation technologies such as VMware or Hyper-V.
* Backup and recovery solutions.
* Endpoint security, firewall management and patch management.
* IT monitoring and ticketing tools.

Candidate Requirements

* 4–7 years of experience in System Administration or IT Infrastructure.
* Experience supporting enterprise IT environments.
* Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
* Knowledge of IT security practices and infrastructure management.
* Good communication and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to manage incidents independently and work within defined SLAs.

Preferred Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT or a related discipline.
* Certifications such as Microsoft Azure, Windows Server, CCNA or VMware are an advantage.
* Experience managing IT infrastructure for a 200+ employee organisation.

Key Expectation: Own the organisation's IT infrastructure, ensure system availability, maintain security standards and deliver reliable technology support across the business.

title: Alpha Nodus - Business & Product Analyst
description:
**About Alpha Nodus**
Alpha Nodus builds Gravity, an AI-powered operations platform for outpatient diagnostic imaging centers and radiology practices in the U.S. Gravity takes on work that imaging centers still do by hand: reading faxed orders, checking insurance, getting prior authorizations, scheduling patients and chasing payment. Each of these is a product line with its own customers, payers, workflows and problems.
  
  
**The Role**
You'll own the health of one Gravity product line at a time, starting with prior authorization. You'll learn how that work really happens at our customers, find where it breaks and why, turn what you find into a short, ranked list of what our team should do next, and keep track of whether it worked. The job is part business analyst, part product analyst. You'll spend as much time with customers' staff, support tickets and real cases as you do in SQL. Your output isn't a dashboard. It's decisions and action items that make a product line work better for the imaging centers that use it.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Go deep on a product line (about 40%):
* Learn the workflow end to end: how an imaging center gets a prior authorization today, payer by payer, from the order arriving to approval or denial.
* Read real cases, sit in on customer calls and talk to the people doing the work, so you understand the problem before you open a chart.
* Find where work stalls and why: payer rules, missing clinical information, referring-office habits, gaps in our product, or how a customer uses it.
* Size every problem in numbers: how often it happens, how much time it costs, and what it means for the center's revenue and its patients.
* Turn findings into action (about 30%):
* Turn what you find into clear, ranked action items. Each has an owner (product, engineering, customer success or the customer), the evidence behind it, and the number that will tell us it worked.
* Write requirements engineering can build from: the problem, the evidence, the user story, acceptance criteria and edge cases.
* Follow through. Check in with owners, push for decisions, and close the loop when a fix ships.
* Bring short, decision-ready findings to customer reviews and product planning.
* Keep a tab on performance (about 20%):
* Define the metrics that show whether a product line is working, such as turnaround time, first-pass approval rate, denial rate by payer, automation rate, staff touches per case and customer adoption. Write them down so everyone reads them the same way.
* Review them every week, catch drops early, and explain what changed before anyone has to ask.
* Report each product line's health to the founder and the team, along with what you're doing about it.
* Help our AI get better (about 10%):
* Gravity's AI agents do much of this work. Because you'll know what the right outcome looks like, you'll build and refresh the test sets we use to evaluate them: real cases labeled with the correct outcome, covering the payers and edge cases that matter.
* Review where the agents go wrong with engineering, and feed those cases back into your action list.

**What You'll Bring**

* 4 - 7 years as a business analyst, product analyst or operations analyst, ideally including time at a product company or startup.
* A track record of going into a messy process or product area, finding what's really going wrong, and getting a team to fix it. You can tell us the before and after in numbers.
* Strong SQL and spreadsheet skills. You pull and check your own numbers rather than waiting for someone else to.
* Experience with a BI tool such as QuickSight, Metabase, Power BI or Tableau.
* Experience mapping processes and writing requirements or user stories.
* A habit of reading raw cases and talking to the people doing the work before trusting a dashboard.
* Clear writing: a one-page finding for a customer, and an action list a team can execute.
* Comfort influencing people you don't manage, and pushing back with evidence.
* Willingness to work U.S. business hours with U.S. customers.

**Nice To Have**

* U.S. healthcare operations experience: prior authorization, eligibility, revenue cycle, payer policies or denials management.
* Experience in radiology, imaging or another operations-heavy healthcare setting.
* Product analytics tools such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or PostHog, and basic Python for analysis.
* Labeling data or reviewing outputs from AI or LLM-based products.
* Working with HIPAA-regulated data.

**What This Role Is Not**
This isn't a data engineering or machine learning role. You won't build data pipelines, run a warehouse or train models; our engineering team owns that. If your best work is building ETL or data platforms, this probably isn't the right fit, and we'd rather say so up front.
  
  
**Why This Role**
You'll own outcomes, not reports. A product line's performance is yours to understand and improve. Your action items go straight to the team that builds the product, and you'll see them ship. You'll see how AI agents are built, measured and improved in production, and you'll help decide what "correct" means. You'll work closely with the founder and with U.S. imaging centers, in a field where getting this right means patients get scanned office, working U.S. hours.
  
  
**Reports To**
Founder / Head of - 7 years.

**Customer Engagement**

•Solution Defence: Collaborate with Pre-Sales and Account Management to present the migration roadmap to anxious enterprise customers, validating the technical integrity and security of the Nutanix platform.

•Workload Assessment: Conduct deep-dive discovery of customer environments to identify dependencies, risks, and hard-coded configurations that could break during migration to Nutanix AHV.

Business Introduction
  
  
GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.
  
  
Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.
  
  
Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.
  
  
**Job Purpose**
The Site Reliability Engineer improves the reliability, resilience and observability of GSK's platforms as a hands-on engineer, reducing toil, preventing incidents and meeting agreed reliability targets. The role defines and monitors SLOs, instruments platforms for observability, leads incident response through to permanent prevention, and applies AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing. It also coaches platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline.
  
  
The role sits in Reliability Engineering & Operations and is deployed into a platform domain while drawing on the central capability, so it holds the central reliability standard inside a team it does not report to. Platform build and engineering direction sit with the Principal Engineers and the Engineering Director, the major incident process sits with the Major Incident Manager, and the reliability standard itself is set by the Reliability Engineering Senior Director. Reliability targets are held jointly with the Platform Manager rather than imposed on them.
  
  
**SCALE AND COMPLEXITY**
This is a senior enterprise reliability leadership role operating across globally distributed, business-critical Productivity and Collaboration services. The post holder is accountable for setting technical direction, resolving systemic and ambiguous reliability risks, and influencing prioritisation across multiple platform teams, suppliers and geographies without relying on direct line authority.
  
  
Leads reliability outcomes for globally consumed productivity, messaging, collaboration and meeting services. The role manages systemic dependencies across identity, security, information governance, network connectivity, endpoint experience, Microsoft 365 services and strategic suppliers, where disruption can affect broad populations across regions and markets.
  
  
The role manages a portfolio of interdependent services with material operational, regulatory, cyber, resilience and financial consequences. It shapes investment and supplier decisions and may influence or govern an annual technology and service portfolio of up to approximately GBP 25 million, where applicable to the assigned scope. Final financial accountability and delegated authority must be confirmed through the Rewards and Finance calibration process.
  
  
**MARKET SCOPE**
Global scope, supporting business operations across regions, countries and markets in which GSK operates. The role establishes consistent reliability outcomes across regional delivery teams while accommodating local regulatory, data-residency, business-continuity and market-criticality requirements.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Define and monitor SLOs for the platforms served, and instrument those platforms for observability so reliability is measured rather than assumed.
* Apply AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing, so that recurring conditions are handled without human intervention.
* Lead incident response for the platforms served, and drive root-cause resolution through to permanent prevention rather than closing on restoration.
* Improve resilience through capacity, failover and recovery engineering, and test recovery rather than documenting it.
* Reduce operational toil through automation and reusable tooling, working the identified manual task and toil candidates and evidencing the effort removed.
* Close observability coverage gaps for the platforms served, prioritising by the reliability risk each gap leaves unmeasured.
* Coach platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline, so reliability is built in rather than inspected in.
* Track reliability metrics against SLOs and team OKRs, and act on the trend rather than only reporting it.
* Support reliability oversight of supplier-run services, holding partner-operated components to the same SLOs as internal ones.
* Hold the central reliability standard while deployed in a platform domain, escalating to the Reliability Engineering Senior Director where local pressure would erode it.
* Feed reliability evidence into the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, so that resilience work competes on stated risk rather than on goodwill.
* Hold the boundaries with the Principal Engineers on platform build, the Major Incident Manager on the major incident process, and the Platform Manager on the reliability targets the platform commits to.
* Set the multi-year reliability strategy and engineering roadmap for the Productivity and Colloboration portfolio, translating enterprise risk and business priorities into funded reliability outcomes.
* Own cross-platform reliability governance, including service tiering, SLO policy, error-budget decisions, resilience exceptions and common engineering standards across internal and supplier-operated services.
* Lead resolution of complex, high-impact and systemic failure modes spanning cloud, hosting, network, security, applications and third-party dependencies, with authority to convene senior technical and service leaders.
* Provide evidence-based recommendations for investment, risk acceptance and supplier performance decisions, including prioritisation across a material service portfolio and, where delegated, spend of up to approximately GBP 25 million.
